answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing or renegotiating with them (c1, c4, c6) won't meet the cost objective. Memory c2 indicates switching to a low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding, which aligns with the cost mandate, but with the line at 94% capacity and no buffer, an untested switch risks delivery interruption. Memory c3 shows that adding a second source protected against single-point-of-failure risk during constrained supply, suggesting a guarded, partial switch (rather than full cutover) balances cost savings against delivery risk. Given only one decision slot this cycle and the 14-day contract expiry, I intend to initiate a small-scale, guarded switch to the alternate vendor for a portion of volume to validate cost and reliability before committing fully, while the incumbent relationship lapses without renewal. This preserves optionality for the next review cycle to add second-sourcing or renegotiate depending on how the guarded test performs.
